notes.selection: nearest_component: group the features carrying the road's tigerNames into components by shared vertices, take the one nearest the origin, and fail unless it is under maxDistanceM away and contains every name in tigerNames.
notes.clip: Bounds are true metres, before any compression. Keep the whole TIGER vertices with xMinM <= x <= xMaxM. Never interpolate an end vertex, so every vertex keeps its TIGER lon/lat.
notes.mtfcc: width is paved width in metres. Widths and surfaces are assumed defaults by road class, not surveyed: TIGER records neither.
notes.compressionBands: Empty: the map is true scale. Should a road ever need shortening, a band is one global remap of x, f: the identity on the stretch holding town center, scaled by factor inside a band, a constant shift past it towards town. trueFrom and trueTo are true metres, west to east, with no overlap. z and lon/lat never change. The build fails if a graph node or trestle is inside a band or a band edge is within 1 mm of a kept TIGER vertex, and adds a vertex wherever a kept segment crosses a band edge.

clip.basis: 500 m past the west trestle (x -4160.2) and the Meehan Savoy Rd junction (x 5807.8), rounded out to 10 m. US 80 crosses each bound once. It ends at TIGER vertices x -4663, z 183 and x 6258, z -574.

continuation.basis: TIGER's Adams St ends 870 m from US 80, short of I-20. All three names carry the same geometry from its north end to clipAt, so take that geometry once. clipAt is the road's first contact with an S1630 ramp of the I-20 interchange, 774.0 m on, and TIGER leaves no gap. The road's first shared vertex with I-20 itself is 144.4 m further north.

clip.basis: From Meehan-Savoy Rd over Stuckey's Bridge at true x 6843 and about 1 km past it. TIGER spells it Stucky; the bridge is Stuckey's, and so is TIGER's own Stuckey Bridge Cutoff Rd beside it.
Takes it over the Chunky River Bridge, where he wakes up, and about 430 m past it. Further on it's just woods. TIGER spells it Grifis-Fountain; the sign goes by what the road is called on the map.
Takes it over the tracks and out of town, about 1.2 km.

stuckey_bridge_rd.reason: The opening was drawn with a road this wide, and it has to stay as it was.

opening.basis: World metres from the bridge. The road really turns north 60 m past the river and south-west 50 m before it, and the opening looks straight down it. So in the world it runs along z 0 from west to east, which is as far as the fog lets you see, and curves back onto its real line at the TIGER vertices nearest joinWest and joinEast. Nothing else moves.
